estimate.method: linear-network prediction (copper_emi::conducted), scenario current_limit: flat-top input-current pulses of amplitude 4.5 A (current_peak, the switch current limit: a worst case, not a prediction), through 1 capacitor branch(es), each its own R-L-C with its own connection inductance, with 9.964 nH hot-loop inductance between the current source and the hot capacitor's node into the 50 uH V-network; level is the RMS dBuV of the least-margin harmonic at the worst LISN port (peak = quasi-peak = average for isolated lines); differential mode only; the value is the HIGH end of a band over rule-of-thumb inputs (largest level over 3 case(s)), the margin is the high end's

assumptions: Results are screening evidence: the solver, source harmonics and LISN transfer are checked against hand calculations, but no prediction has been correlated with a measurement and no accuracy figure is claimed.

Linear time-invariant network: all passives are linear; capacitor and inductor parasitics are single-element ESR/ESL/parallel-C models with no frequency dependence (no skin or proximity effect, no ferrite or dielectric dispersion).
The capacitances are used as given: DC-bias and temperature derating of an MLCC (more than half of the capacitance at rated bias) is the caller's input, not part of this model.
measures.common_mode_reason: the only capacitance the board model knows for the switch node is its island capacitance to the board's own ground plane (EMI-SWITCH-NODE), and that plane is the converter's return: the current it carries closes through the plane and the controller's ground pin without entering the LISN, so using it as the capacitance to the LISN reference would overstate common mode by the whole shielding effect of the plane. The capacitance that drives common-mode current out of the board is the one from the board (switch node, heat sink, plane edges, cables) to the reference or chassis, which depends on geometry outside the board model; the reported levels are differential mode only and common mode, which usually dominates above a few MHz, is not included
measures.dc_bias_derating: rule of thumb band; nominal derated
hot_capacitor_sources: ESR 5 mohm default for a ceramic
inputs_text: Vin 12 V (supply VIN on VIN), Vout 5 V (supply VOUT on VOUT), duty 0.4167

scenario current_limit: no load_current is declared on U1: the switch current limit 4.5 A is used as the pulse amplitude, a worst case and not a prediction of operation; declare `load_current = <current>;` on the component to give the cell an operating point

current edge time 5 ns (10-90 %, switch pin rise_time/fall_time), used for the current commutation because no current_rise_time/current_fall_time is declared; ramp 6.25 ns (0-100 %, divided by 0.8); an assumption: the voltage edge and the current commutation are different quantities

capacitor CIN (hot): 10 uF nominal 5 uF, ESR 5 mohm (package default), ESL 0.6 nH (package_default), DC-bias loss (rule of thumb: ceramic DC-bias loss by package (0805: 50 %; 0402, 0603, 0805 50 %, 1206 35 %, 1210 and larger 25 %); the band runs from no loss to this loss, the nominal is the derated value from 5 V hot-supply voltage, else the un-derated value; declare capacitance_at_bias on the component to replace it) (nominal derated); connection: none, the hot-loop inductance 9.964 nH (traced copper path) is in the converter's branch; branch current over source current 100.0 % at the fundamental and 100.0 % at the worst harmonic

hot-loop inductance sits between the converter's current source and the hot capacitor's node K, where the capacitors and the feed attach: it does not change the level at the LISN (an ideal current source is not affected by a series inductance); a feed attached at the switch pins instead of the capacitor pads would put it in series with the capacitor
no anti-resonance of the input network between 150 kHz and 30 MHz (prominence of at least 0.5 dB)
common mode not modelled: the island capacitance to the board's ground plane is not a path to the LISN reference

estimate.definition: 20 log10(f C V / (100 MHz * 1 pF * 1 V)), maximised over 30 MHz to 1 GHz: f the frequency, C the island capacitance to the nearest ground plane, V the amplitude of the switch-node trapezoid envelope at f. The displacement current 2 pi f C V is the driver; no field-per-current constant and no distance enter, so the score ranks cells and boards by drive and is neither a field nor comparable with an emission limit. Relative to the reference product only
estimate.method: ranking score 20 log10(f C V / (100 MHz * 1 pF * 1 V)), V the trapezoid envelope of a 12 V swing (500000 Hz fixed, edge 5 ns (10-90 %, switch pin rise_time/fall_time), duty 0.42 from 5 V / 12 V), C the island capacitance to the ground plane, worst point of 30 MHz to 1 GHz; relative, not a field, no distance, no limit
not_modelled: cable and attached-conductor geometry (length, routing, which conductors the displacement current reaches)
board-to-environment coupling (capacitance of the board to chassis, earth or a heat sink)
return impedance of the common-mode path (the plane under the island is the converter's own return)
radiation efficiency of the structure that carries the current
frequency dependence of the island capacitance (a quasi-static plate-and-fringe estimate)

limits.limit_source: CISPR 32 / EN 55032 radiated 30-1000 MHz (Annex A; table number unverified)
notes: screening evidence: ranks likely noise sources, never establishes EMC qualification

validated: the closed forms, the circuit solver and the receiver emulation against hand calculations and analytic cases (unit tests); not validated: no estimate has been correlated with a measurement, so no accuracy, confidence interval or bound is claimed; margins are screening margins, not pass or fail

uncertainty is reported as three separate things per estimate: numerical sensitivity (null for closed forms), parameter bands from rule-of-thumb defaults (band_db), and the named mechanisms not modelled (not_modelled)
common-mode radiation is a relative coupling-risk score (ranking only): it has no distance, no field value and no margin, and is never compared with an emission limit
hot-loop geometry is the traced copper path where routed copper joins the loop pads (traced_copper, partially_traced) and the pad-centre polygon elsewhere (placement_estimate)

differential-mode loop field is free space; in the current_limit scenario the radiated sweep is the upper envelope of the trapezoid, in the declared_operating_point scenario it is the harmonic lines of the ramp-on-pedestal switch current; peak against quasi-peak limits
limit tables are transcribed from the published numbers and must be verified against the standards

radiated hot-loop estimates are ordered by their headline level in dBuV/m, each in its own cell's scenario (declared_operating_point or current_limit); levels of unlike scenarios are compared as numbers, not as like with like: a current_limit level is a worst case that bounds the cell, a declared_operating_point level an estimate of its operation (ties break by loop area, larger first)
